title: Stylohyoid ligament
summary: The stylohyoid ligament is a ligament that connects the hyoid bone to the temporal styloid process (of the temporal bone of the skull).

sections.heading: Structure
paragraphs: The stylohyoid ligament connects the lesser horn of hyoid bone to the styloid process of the temporal bone of the skull.

sections.heading: Clinical significance
paragraphs: The stylohyoid ligament frequently contains a little cartilage in its center, which is sometimes partially ossified in Eagle syndrome.

sections.heading: Other animals
paragraphs: In many animals, the epihyal is a distinct bone in the centre of the stylohyoid ligament, which is similar to that seen in Eagle syndrome.
